title: Constructible module sheaves generate the category
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ (an object of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) is a quotient of a coproduct of constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]: there are a set $I$, constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $C_i$ ($i\in I$) whose coproduct $\bigoplus_{i\in I}C_i$ exists in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}C_i\to F$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.

proof.text: Use affine_etale_rankOne_isSeparating for the family G of rank-one extensions indexed by all affine etale objects. This realizes the original affine generator step directly in the ModuleCat-valued sheaf category; no passage to ringed-site SheafOfModules is needed.

For F, let I be the dependent sum of b in this family and morphisms G_b -> F. Set C_(b,a)=G_b. An affine source is compact and quasi-separated; apply isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_etaleLowerShriek_constant with M=ModuleCat.of Lambda Lambda to every summand.

Install the existing small-etale sheafification instance, then Mathlib Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize yields HasCoproduct C. Define pi=Sigma.desc of the indexed morphisms. For pi >> f=pi >> g, precompose with Sigma.ι C (b,a) to obtain a >> f=a >> g. The separating-family theorem gives f=g, proving Epi pi. Package I, C, constructibility, HasCoproduct and pi as the required witnesses.
